response.rationale:
These look like two separate concepts. They are related, but they are not the same thing under different names.

A, the Booking, is an individual booking. BookingService calls BookingRepository.findActiveByMembership and HireStockRepository.get, which ties a booking to one member and to hire equipment. It also checks SessionService.availability before creating a booking.

B, the Club Booking, has its own repository, ClubBookingRepository, holding a Map<string, ClubBooking>. It also has its own service, ClubBookingService, which offers an invoice operation. SessionService.effectiveCapacity reads it, which suggests a club booking is a group reservation that holds back session capacity and is billed to the club. There is no sign of a link to a membership.

So the two have different repositories, services and lifecycles (pending or active membership bookings versus invoiced club reservations). Both are kinds of booking against a session, but each models its own real-world thing. I only have the slice shown here, so this rests on the call graph and names rather than the full class definitions.
